title.es: Leer el ambiente de la conversación

es: Reconocer aperturas, señales de interés, cambios de tema y cierres en conversaciones informales entre desconocidos, e inferir por el tono y las pistas si alguien quiere seguir hablando.

teaching.en: 'What brought you to the book fair tonight?' is a safe opener, because it asks about the shared context and never feels like an interrogation.
teaching.es: «¿Qué te trajo esta noche a la feria del libro?» es una apertura segura, porque pregunta por el contexto compartido y nunca parece un interrogatorio.
teaching.explanationEs: Un opener pregunta por algo que ambos ven o viven: es ligero y fácil de contestar.

it asks about the shared context and never feels like an interrogation.

teaching.en: At a wedding you mingle for hours, so you will often strike up a conversation with an acquaintance of the couple and exchange pleasantries about the venue first.
teaching.es: En una boda socializas durante horas, así que a menudo entablarás conversación con un conocido de la pareja y empezarás intercambiando cortesías sobre el local.
teaching.explanationEs: Strike up a conversation = empezarla con alguien; pleasantries son comentarios corteses sin compromiso.

teaching.en: She sounded genuine when she answered, 'Oh, really? How did that happen?', whereas a listener who only murmurs 'Right' gives you nothing to build on.
teaching.es: Sonaba sincera cuando respondió: «¿Ah, sí? ¿Cómo pasó eso?», mientras que quien solo murmura «Ya» no te da nada sobre lo que continuar.
teaching.explanationEs: El interés genuino se oye en el eco y en la pregunta de detalle; el desinterés, en respuestas secas.
segments: She sounded genuine when she answered, 'Oh, really? How did that happen?', whereas
a listener who only murmurs 'Right' gives you nothing to build on.

teaching.en: A one-word answer followed by a quick glance at the phone is a cue that the person wants to leave, so learn to read the room before you start a long story.
teaching.es: Una respuesta de una palabra seguida de una mirada rápida al celular es una señal de que la persona quiere irse, así que aprende a captar el ambiente antes de empezar una historia larga.
teaching.explanationEs: Cue es una pista; read the room significa interpretar el estado de ánimo del grupo.

person wants to leave, so learn to read the room before you start a long story.
teaching.audioText: A one-word answer followed by a quick glance at the phone is a cue that the person wants to leave, so learn to read the room before you start a long story.

teaching.en: If the conversation turns awkward, steer it back to something neutral, such as the food or the music, instead of pressing on with the same subject.
teaching.es: Si la conversación se vuelve incómoda, reconduce hacia algo neutro, como la comida o la música, en lugar de insistir con el mismo tema.
teaching.explanationEs: Steer it back = volver con suavidad a un tema cómodo; no hace falta explicar el silencio.

teaching.en: A warm closing is brief and gives a reason, as in 'It was great chatting, but I'll let you get back to your friends,' and only skilled listeners pick up on it.
teaching.es: Un cierre cálido es breve y da un motivo, como en «Fue genial charlar, pero te dejo volver con tus amigos», y solo los buenos oyentes lo captan.
teaching.explanationEs: El cierre agradece, justifica y no se alarga; pick up on = darse cuenta de algo que no se dice abiertamente.

prompt.es: Clasifica lo que dice un desconocido a otro visitante de la feria.

choices.text: A cue of genuine interest in a detail she just gave
An opener that uses something both people can see
A closing that gives a polite reason to leave

feedback.es: Nadie ha hablado aún: el desconocido arranca con un objeto compartido (el libro) y una pregunta fácil, lo propio de una apertura.

hint.es: Fíjate en si ya había una conversación antes de esa frase.

origin.text: At the book fair, a stranger beside the coffee stall turns to a woman and says: 'I couldn't help noticing you've picked up the same novel I've been looking for all year. Is it any good?'

prompt.es: Completa: «Era una señal clara de que quería terminar la conversación.»

feedback.es: Cue es la pista o señal que revela lo que alguien siente sin decirlo; aquí, las respuestas de una sola sílaba y la mirada a la puerta.

hint.es: Es una pista que te ayuda a leer la situación.

origin.text: Mia answered in single syllables, looked down at her phone and glanced at the door. It was a clear ___ that she wanted the conversation to end.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Me encantaría saber más, pero te dejo que sigas socializando.»

answer.text: I'd love to hear more, but I'll let you mingle

feedback.es: La despedida cálida combina el interés («I'd love to hear more») con un motivo para cerrar («I'll let you mingle»).

hint.es: Empieza por el deseo y termina con el motivo para cerrar.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué señal llevó a la narradora a marcharse.

choices.text: He started talking about the cake instead of the flat.
He said he had to go back to the rest of his family.
His replies got shorter while he kept looking at his phone.

feedback.es: Las respuestas cada vez más cortas y las miradas al celular son las señales que la narradora dice haber captado antes de despedirse.

origin.audio: At my cousin's wedding I ended up at a table next to a man I had never met. I opened with a simple question about how he knew the bride, and he said they had once shared a flat in college. I repeated his words, six people in one flat, and he laughed and told me the whole story. Ten minutes later, though, he began checking his phone, and his answers got shorter and shorter. I took the hint, thanked him for the story and went off to find the cake.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase de una boda con su función en la conversación.

pairs: What brought you to the book fair tonight?
Six languages? How did you manage that?
Speaking of food, have you tried the cake?
I'll let you mingle, it was lovely talking to you.

feedback.es: Cada frase lleva su marca: pregunta de contexto, eco con detalle, enlace «Speaking of…» y despedida con motivo y buenos deseos.

pairs: What brought you to the book fair tonight?
Six languages? How did you manage that?
Speaking of food, have you tried the cake?
I'll let you mingle, it was lovely talking to you.

prompt.es: Decide qué función cumple la frase de esta invitada al entrar en la sala.

choices.text: An opener that mentions a shared situation and invites a reply
A change of topic that moves away from something they were discussing
A closing that thanks the listener and gives a reason to leave

feedback.es: No había conversación previa: la invitada abre con una observación compartida y una pregunta con humor que pide respuesta.

origin.text: A guest approaches another guest she has never spoken to, nods towards the dance floor and says: 'You've been standing by the window for a while. Are you waiting for someone, or hiding from the dancing like I am?'

prompt.es: Escucha el recuerdo de Tom y elige qué se deduce del final de la charla.

choices.text: She felt offended by his question about what had surprised her most.
She enjoyed the chat but used the talk as a polite exit.
She wanted to keep talking but could not find her friends in time.

feedback.es: Tras responder con calidez a sus preguntas, ella mira el reloj y alega la charla y sus amigos: un cierre cortés, no un enojo.

origin.audio: Tom recalls a conversation at the book fair. The woman beside him said she had been writing novels for thirty years. He replied, thirty years? That must take patience, and she smiled and told him about her first book. He asked what had surprised her most about the job. She paused, looked at her watch and said she should really find her friends before the talk began. Tom laughed it off, but he never saw her again.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige con qué fin repite Tom «thirty years?».

choices.text: To doubt that her claim could possibly be true.
To steer the conversation politely towards another subject.
To show interest and invite her to say more.

feedback.es: Repetir el dato y añadir «That must take patience» es un eco admirado: ella responde contando su primer libro, es decir, amplía.

origin.audio: Tom recalls a conversation at the book fair. The woman beside him said she had been writing novels for thirty years. He replied, thirty years? That must take patience, and she smiled and told him about her first book. He asked what had surprised her most about the job. She paused, looked at her watch and said she should really find her friends before the talk began. Tom laughed it off, but he never saw her again.

prompt.es: Completa: «No supo captar las señales de que ella había dejado de escuchar.»

feedback.es: Pick up on significa darse cuenta de algo que no se dice abiertamente, como una señal de desinterés.

origin.text: Mia was standing by the wall, looking at her messages. Tom kept talking, but he failed to ___ up on the signs that she had stopped listening.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Intercambiaron cortesías antes de pasar a algo más personal.»

answer.text: They exchanged pleasantries before moving on to something more personal

feedback.es: Pleasantries son las cortesías iniciales; la secuencia «before moving on to» marca el paso a un tema más personal.

prompt.es: Lee el mensaje de Leo y elige qué actitud transmite hacia Ana.

choices.text: Honest and a little worried, yet keen to talk again.
Offended that she showed so little interest in his stories.
Careless about whether the evening went well for her.

feedback.es: Leo reconoce que habla mucho, se pregunta si se alargó demasiado y aun así propone seguir otro día: autocrítica con ganas de repetir.

origin.text: Dear Ana, thank you for a lovely evening. I hope I didn't keep you too long: I tend to talk a lot when I'm nervous. I noticed you kept glancing towards the food table, so I wonder whether I talked for too long. Either way, it was lovely to meet you, and I'd enjoy hearing the end of your story some other time.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hace el hablante con «enough about me».

choices.text: He ends the chat politely and heads for the exit.
He stops talking about himself and hands the turn over.
He switches to a different topic because he has nothing left to say.

feedback.es: Se disculpa por haber hablado tanto y devuelve el turno con una pregunta abierta: reequilibra la charla, no la cierra.

origin.audio: I'm so sorry, I've been going on about my search for a flat for ages. Enough about me! Are you here for the talk, or just browsing the stalls?

prompt.es: Completa: «Lo más fácil es entablar conversación comentando algo que todos ven.»

feedback.es: Strike up a conversation es la colocación para iniciarla con alguien que no conoces, a menudo con un comentario sobre lo compartido.

origin.text: Nobody at the table knew each other, and the silence was getting heavy. The easiest way to ___ up a conversation is to comment on something you can all see, like the music.
